title: Kickstarter lightning strikes
summary: Eric Migicovsky launches Pebble on Kickstarter with a $100k goal. It becomes the most-funded project in Kickstarter history — $10.27M from 68,929 backers.

title: First Pebbles ship
summary: After manufacturing hurdles, the original black-and-white e-paper Pebble starts shipping. Always-on screen, week-long battery, four buttons — a new category is born.

title: Pebble Steel arrives
summary: A stainless-steel premium Pebble with a glass screen. Proof the brand could do dress watches without killing battery life.

title: Pebble Time Kickstarter
summary: Color Sharp Memory LCD, microphone, Timeline UI. Another record-breaking Kickstarter — the Time series defines the golden era of Pebble.

title: Pebble Time Round
summary: The thinnest, lightest round Pebble. Stylish and beloved — and famously fiddly when the tiny battery eventually dies.

title: Pebble 2 & Pebble 2 HR
summary: Heart-rate sensing lands on a B&W Pebble. Over two million watches sold across the brand's lifetime.

title: Fitbit acquires Pebble assets
summary: Hardware production stops. The planned Time 2 and Pebble Core are cancelled. Software IP moves to Fitbit; Kickstarter refunds for unshipped Pebble 2s.

title: Rebble keeps the lights on
summary: Fitbit shuts original cloud services. Rebble Web Services take over the appstore, Timeline, weather, dictation, and firmware — community-funded survival.

title: Google acquires Fitbit
summary: PebbleOS source quietly sits inside Google. The community keeps legacy hardware alive while hoping the code might someday be freed.

title: Google open-sources PebbleOS
summary: Most of the classic firmware lands on GitHub. Chipset/BT bits stripped — but the door to a real comeback swings open.

title: Core Devices opens pre-orders
summary: Eric returns with Core 2 Duo and Core Time 2 — open-source PebbleOS, weeks of battery, 10,000+ existing apps. The dream watch that was cancelled in 2016 gets a second life.

title: Pebble name returns
summary: Core Devices recovers the Pebble trademark. Core 2 Duo and Core Time 2 become Pebble 2 Duo and Pebble Time 2.

title: Rebble × Core partnership
summary: Shared appstore backend. Devs publish once; apps appear for legacy Rebble users and new Core watches. The ecosystem stays unified.

title: Pebble Round 2 announced
summary: A stylish round successor at $199 — stainless frame, 1.3" 64-color e-paper, touch + buttons. Pre-orders open.

title: Time 2 enters mass production
summary: 20,000+ pre-orders. 30m water resistance on the line. First units ship late March; production ramps toward 500/day.

title: Time 2 in stock worldwide
summary: Pre-order backlog cleared. Pebble Time 2 ships within 48 hours from rePebble.com — 93 countries and counting.

title: Round 2 starts shipping
summary: Factory batches leave Asia. Soft launch ramps while software (PebbleOS + mobile app) keeps getting weekly love — plugins, WASM watchfaces in the browser, and more.

title: Index 01 in stock
summary: All ring sizes ship within 48 hours from rePebble.com — voice-capture “external memory” hardware joins Time 2 on the buy-it-now list.

title: Plugins land in the production SDK
summary: Headless phone-side Plugins graduate from preview to `pebble sdk install latest` and CloudPebble — watchfaces and apps can pull shared data (weather, location, home control) with a new permissions model.

title: Rebble elects a new board
summary: First community board election wraps — David Wise stays president, JP joins, and the foundation sets goals for hackathons and life in the Pebble 2.0 era.
